title_prefix: estimaterawfee omits decay and scale and
mechanism: Confirmed, with one correction and two additions. Core's estimaterawfee (rpc/fees.cpp:169-215) builds each horizon object in two branches. Success (feeRate != CFeeRate(0)): feerate, decay, scale, pass, and fail only when buckets.fail.start != -1. Failure: decay, scale, fail (the default EstimatorBucket, all -1/0 per block_policy_estimator.h:72-80), the errors array, and NO feerate key, because CFeeRate(0) is the error sentinel. decay and scale are declared WITHOUT /*optional=*/true in the RPCResult (rpc/fees.cpp:120-121) while feerate, pass, fail and errors are all optional, and Core enforces that declaration at run time: RPCHelpMan::HandleRequest re-checks the returned object against m_results whenever -rpcdoccheck is set (rpc/util.cpp:662-681), and the functional test framework writes rpcdoccheck=1 into every node's config (test/functional/test_framework/util.py:561). So in Core decay and scale are present in every horizon object of every estimaterawfee response a functional test ever sees. Ours (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:916-962) builds the horizon object from feerate, pass, fail and errors only. Correction to the record: decay and scale are NOT missing from the tree -- tx-confirm-stats-estimate-median already returns them in the EstimationResult plist (src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:325, probed as :DECAY 0.962d0 :SCALE 1 for the short horizon), so the values exist and the RPC handler simply drops them. Addition 1: the omission is in BOTH branches, not only the no-answer one -- a populated estimator's successful horizon object also lacks decay and scale. Addition 2: our no-answer branch emits ("feerate" . 0.0d0) and omits the fail bucket when the estimator recorded none, where Core omits feerate and always emits fail; and our errors string is "Insufficient data or no feerate found" against Core's "Insufficient data or no feerate found which meets threshold".
consequence: Kept at S3. estimaterawfee is in Core's `hidden` command category and its own help text opens with "WARNING: This interface is unstable and may disappear or change!", so it is a diagnostic surface rather than the fee source a wallet spends from -- that is estimatesmartfee, which is a separate finding. The harm is therefore to whoever is trying to understand an estimate, and it is real: decay and scale are two of the five things this RPC exists to report, they are what tells an operator which horizon's moving average is dominating and at what resolution the target was rounded, and a reader who sees "feerate": 0 cannot tell a genuinely-zero answer from "this horizon had nothing to say" -- the distinction Core encodes by omitting the key. A Core-parity client that reads e["decay"] gets a KeyError against this node on every call. No client acts on a wrong fee here: the divergent value is 0, which is not a fee anything would pay (a transaction built at it would be refused below the relay minimum), so this stays below the money bar for S2. On functional tests: no Core test asserts on decay or scale (grep over test/functional returns nothing), and feature_fee_estimation.py's check_raw_estimates only reads e["feerate"] and asserts it greater than zero -- which would fail here for a horizon with no answer, but would KeyError in Core for the same horizon, so that assertion does not cleanly separate the two implementations. The mechanical Core-side check that DOES separate them is -rpcdoccheck, which every functional test run has on.
evidence: Two probes in build/ga11v (worktree fix/ga11v-rpcutil-s3a, warm image bitcoin-lisp-dev-e618132ea0cf), both through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method with %normalize-rpc-params. (1) p-fees.lisp, fresh empty estimator: estimaterawfee(2) => {"short": {"feerate": 0.0d0, "errors": ["Insufficient data or no feerate found"]}, "medium": same, "long": same} -- no decay, no scale, no fail bucket, and a feerate key Core would not emit. estimaterawfee(2, 0.5) identical. estimaterawfee(25) omits the short horizon entirely (short max_confirms 12, medium 48, long 1008), which matches Core's `continue`. estimaterawfee(1009) => -8 "Invalid conf_target, must be between 1 and 1008", matching rpc_estimatefee.py:40 verbatim. With bl.mp:*block-policy-estimator* NIL the result is an empty object, as Core's would be. The internal call bl.mp:bpe-estimate-raw-fee(2, 0.95, :short) returned (0 (:PASS NIL :FAIL NIL :DECAY 0.962d0 :SCALE 1)) -- the values the RPC drops. (2) p-fees2.lisp, a 200-block synthetic replay (40 transactions per block at 10000 and 25000 sat/kvB, each block confirming the previous block's set) so the success branch is reached: estimaterawfee(2) => short/medium/long each with feerate and a pass bucket (startrange 9813, endrange 24797, withintarget 526.08, totalconfirmed 526.08, inmempool 0.0, leftmempool 0.0 for short) and STILL no decay and no scale. estimaterawfee(1) on the same estimator mixes the branches: short is the no-answer case and emits "feerate": 0.0 alongside a fail bucket and the errors array, where Core would emit decay, scale, fail and errors and no feerate. One further divergence surfaced by that fail bucket: its endrange came back as the 99-digit integer 999999999999999967336168804116691273849533185806555472917961779471295845921727862608739868455469056, the CL ROUND of the 1e99 infinity bucket, where Core's round() keeps a double and UniValue renders it as an exponent-form number (INF_FEERATE = 1e99, refs/bitcoin/src/policy/fees/block_policy_estimator.cpp:39,553). Files: src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:905-962; src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:225-325,576-609; refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/fees.cpp:97-215; refs/bitcoin/src/policy/fees/block_policy_estimator.h:72-89; refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/util.cpp:662-681; refs/bitcoin/test/functional/test_framework/util.py:561.
fix_shape: Reshape the horizon object to Core's two branches and stop inventing a zero. In src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp's estimaterawfee, take decay and scale out of the plist bl.mp:bpe-estimate-raw-fee already returns (:DECAY, :SCALE at src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:325) and push them into the object FIRST in both branches, unconditionally. Then split on the same sentinel Core uses -- rate zero means no answer, not a zero fee: on a non-zero rate emit feerate, decay, scale, pass, and fail only when the fail bucket's start is not the -1 sentinel; on a zero rate emit decay, scale, fail and errors and NO feerate key, materialising the default all -1 bucket when the estimator recorded none so the key is always there. Change the error string to Core's exact "Insufficient data or no feerate found which meets threshold". While there, make %raw-fee-bucket-json render the range endpoints the way Core's round()-on-double does rather than with CL ROUND, so the infinity bucket comes out as 1e99 and not as a 99-digit integer. Give the pass/fail plists an explicit -1 start/end default instead of the current NIL so the sentinel test is a comparison rather than a null check. Test it with two rows against a driven estimator -- one horizon with an answer, one without -- asserting the exact KEY SET of each horizon object, since the whole finding is about which keys are present; keep an empty-estimator run as the positive control so the key-set assertion cannot pass vacuously.
